pre_condition: value is None or a string.
post_condition:
Returns a non-empty string. The input is sanitized first: None becomes an empty string; any non-None value is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace and lowercased. Behavior by sanitized-input class:
(1) Default — When the sanitized input is empty or case-insensitively matches any string in a fixed, closed set of falsy sentinel values, returns the canonical default backend name.
(2) Auto-detect — When the sanitized input case-insensitively equals "auto", returns the literal string "auto".
(3) Known alias — When the sanitized input matches a key in a fixed alias-to-canonical-name lookup table, returns the mapped canonical name. The mapping is idempotent: every canonical name is a key that maps to itself. All distinct aliases that identify the same backend map to the identical canonical name string.
(4) Unrecognized — When the sanitized input falls into none of the above classes, the sanitized input itself is returned unchanged.
In cases (1) and (3), the return value is always a member of a closed set of canonical backend identifier strings.
